transport-noise.name: Long-term harmful noise (road, rail and air traffic)
transport-noise.passage: at least one in five people in the EU are exposed to long-term noise levels considered harmful to their health. About 92 million people are exposed to harmful day-evening-night noise levels caused by road traffic.

who-environment.name: WHO fact sheets: environmental causes of death and disease

ambient-air.name: Ambient (outdoor) air pollution
ambient-air.passage: In 2019, 99% of the world's population was living in places where the WHO air quality guidelines levels were not met. Ambient (outdoor) air pollution is estimated to have caused 4.2 million premature deaths worldwide in 2019.

household-air.name: Household air pollution
household-air.passage: Around 2.1 billion people worldwide (around a quarter of the global population) cook using open fires or inefficient stoves. Household air pollution was responsible for an estimated 2.9 million deaths per year in 2021

unsafe-water.name: Contaminated drinking water
unsafe-water.passage: In 2022, globally, at least 1.7 billion people use a drinking water source contaminated with faeces.

heat.name: Extreme heat
heat.passage: Between 2000–2019 studies show approximately 489 000 heat-related deaths occur each year

lead.name: Lead exposure
lead.passage: Lead exposure was attributed to more than 3.5 million deaths globally in 2023, primarily due to cardiovascular effects.

who-environment.note: IHME GBD risk-factor tables were not opened; WHO fact sheets stand in for the cause-of-burden list.

sdg.name: UN Sustainable Development Goals: targets bearing on the environment

6.1.name: Target 6.1

6.2.name: Target 6.2
6.2.passage: By 2030, achieve access to adequate and equitable sanitation and hygiene for all and end open defecation

6.3.name: Target 6.3

6.4.name: Target 6.4
6.4.passage: By 2030, substantially increase water-use efficiency across all sectors and ensure sustainable withdrawals

6.6.name: Target 6.6
6.6.passage: By 2020, protect and restore water-related ecosystems, including mountains, forests, wetlands, rivers, aquifers and lakes

7.1.name: Target 7.1

11.4.passage: Strengthen efforts to protect and safeguard the world’s cultural and natural heritage

11.5.name: Target 11.5
11.5.passage: By 2030, significantly reduce the number of deaths and the number of people affected

11.6.name: Target 11.6
11.6.passage: By 2030, reduce the adverse per capita environmental impact of cities

11.7.name: Target 11.7
11.7.passage: By 2030, provide universal access to safe, inclusive and accessible, green and public spaces

11.b.passage: By 2020, substantially increase the number of cities and human settlements adopting and implementing integrated policies

12.2.name: Target 12.2
